input: Set up a standing desk treadmill trial at work

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this is a solo personal trial or a broader team/company pilot changes the scale of planning, approvals needed, and number of units required.
Whether the user needs to get buy-in from an employer, facilities manager, or HR determines what permissions, paperwork, or proposals are required.
The physical workspace (open plan, private office, shared area) affects whether a treadmill desk is even feasible and what setup logistics are involved.
The budget cap directly determines whether to buy, rent, or request the equipment, and which models are realistic options.
Knowing whether the user already has equipment or needs to source it sets the immediate next action — research vs. procurement vs. installation.
Understanding what the user wants to get out of the trial (productivity, health metrics, comfort) defines what to track and how to decide if it worked.
The intended trial duration shapes the timeline, milestones, and how formal or lightweight the plan needs to be.

gold.taskTitle: Set up a standing desk treadmill trial at work
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to pilot using a treadmill desk at their workplace, covering everything from sourcing the equipment to actually running the trial.

questions.title: Is this trial just for you or a wider group?
questions.description: Clarifies whether one person or multiple employees are participating, which changes procurement scale and approval complexity.

questions.title: Who at work needs to approve this?
questions.description: Identifies the decision-makers involved — manager, HR, facilities — so the right stakeholders can be approached early.

questions.title: What does your current workspace physically look like?
questions.description: Determines whether the space (private office, open plan desk, shared area) can accommodate a treadmill desk without major changes.

questions.title: What is your budget for sourcing the equipment?
questions.description: Sets financial boundaries to determine whether to buy, rent, or request employer funding for the treadmill desk.

questions.title: Do you already have a treadmill desk or need to source one?
questions.description: Establishes the immediate next action — whether the focus is on research and procurement or on setup and installation.

questions.title: What does a successful trial look like to you?
questions.description: Defines the outcome the user is optimising for — improved focus, step count, back pain reduction — so the trial can be measured meaningfully.

questions.title: How long do you want the trial period to run?
questions.description: Sets the timeline for the experiment, which determines how formal the plan needs to be and when to evaluate results.
